# Contract test fixtures

`fixtures/` holds JSON files that .NET tests write and TypeScript tests read, so that a TypeScript package can be
checked against the .NET package it mirrors. This folder is not a package; it contains only the fixture files.

## What the folder holds

Each directory under `fixtures/` is one catalog, and each file in it is one scenario:
`fixtures/<catalog>/<scenario>.json`. Every file is a JSON envelope:

```json
{
  "$comment": "Synthetic test data; no real PII. Generated by DcsvIo.D2.Tests Integration/ContractFixtures.",
  "data": { "...the values a test compares..." },
  "scenario": "<scenario>"
}
```

A test compares the `data` field. The other fields describe the file. The data is synthetic and holds no personal
data.

`fixtures/mq-consumer-golden/` holds messages encoded by the .NET messaging packages: a plaintext message with its AMQP
headers, and a version-1 encrypted frame. The integration tests in `packages/typescript/messaging/rabbitmq/tests/integration/`
publish them to a RabbitMQ container and check how the TypeScript consumer handles them.

## Which emitters write it

The emitter classes in `packages/dotnet/tests/Integration/ContractFixtures/` write every file. Each class writes the
scenarios of one catalog through `FixturePathHelpers.WriteFixture`, and each emitter method is a test with the trait
`Category=ContractFixtures`. `WriteFixture` sorts the keys of every dictionary it writes and ends lines with LF. A rerun
with no code change writes the same bytes.

Do not edit a fixture by hand. Change the emitter or the code it reads, then regenerate the files from the repository
root:

```bash
dotnet test packages/dotnet/tests/DcsvIo.D2.Tests.csproj -- --filter-trait "Category=ContractFixtures"
```

The path is the one in this repository, where the .NET test project is `packages/dotnet/tests/DcsvIo.D2.Tests.csproj`.
The command needs the .NET SDK and builds the test project before it runs it. The fixture emitters start no container.

Commit the regenerated files with the change that caused them, so the diff shows how the wire output changed.
